page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning includes 161 GB of local SSD storage, while zero GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced single-threaded execution alongside multi-core throughput constrained by the 2-core physical limit. In single-core testing, the instance records a Geekbench score of 1629.0 and a stress-ng score of 1896.69, both placing in the middle performance tier. Single-threaded gzip compression attains 28.32 GB/sec. Conversely, parallelized workloads show lower relative output, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3485.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3871.28. Thread-intensive bzip3 decompression yields 19.32 GB/sec, falling into the bottom decile of tested systems.

Memory subsystem benchmarks show 29.28 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 25.41 GB/sec for large-block writes. Application-level performance reflects the core count constraint, with Redis SET operations achieving 3.97 million operations per second and static web throughput reaching 6.29 GB/sec. In lightweight machine learning inference benchmarks using a 135M model, prompt processing registers 324.48 tokens per second, while text generation maintains an average rate of 113.38 tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high RAM density and local temporary disk capacity against limited compute parallelism. Because 4 vCPUs share 2 physical cores, CPU-intensive parallel operations experience thread contention. However, the qualitative resource balance makes it efficient for memory-heavy tasks requiring modest compute, such as caching tiers, mid-sized relational databases, and data manipulation pipelines requiring fast local scratch storage.

This setup yields an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation paired with 161 GB of integrated local SSD storage, without dedicated graphics hardware. Benchmark measurements show capable single-threaded results, such as an average Geekbench single-core score of 1629.0 and 28.32 GB/sec in gzip compression. Multi-threaded throughput reflects hardware limits from its 2 physical cores, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 3485.0, static web throughput of 6.29 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput of 3.97 million operations per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 29.28 GB/sec. The E4ds_v5 fits memory-intensive, moderate-compute workloads such as in-memory caches, small-to-medium databases, and search indexes requiring local scratch disk performance.
